errors: No mathematical error is visible. The use of R_a ∧ R_{a'} rather than Isom(R_a, R_{a'}) is consistent with the orientation reversal of the gluing map (orientation reversal inverts the torsor). The remark that 'the structure: repères follows in a less obvious way' is left unexplained, so there is a gap rather than an error.

ideas.what: Gluing ('recollement') of marked surfaces along pairs of marked boundary circles as the key non-tautological operation building the Teichmüller tower; combinatorially, joining free edges of a vertex-weighted dual graph.
ideas.modern_name: Modular operad / stable graph gluing; Lego–Teichmüller game
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984) for the programme; Getzler–Kapranov (1998, modular operads); Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000); Bakalov–Kirillov (2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of the Teichmüller tower and the 'jeu de Lego-Teichmüller'

ideas.what: Boundary circles carry a level r_a and a torsor R_a under Z/r_aZ (discrete 'roots' of a tangential marking). Gluing requires r(a) = r(a'), and the gluing datum is an element of the contracted product R_a ∧_{Z/rZ} R_{a'}, giving r choices.
ideas.modern_name: Balanced twisted nodes with μ_r gluing data (ghost automorphisms) for twisted/orbifold stable curves; also gluing of framed/level-structured boundaries
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abramovich–Vistoli (2002), Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli (2003); Chiodo (r-spin, 2008); for real framings, Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov (1995)
ideas.where_published: Not, to my knowledge, in this torsor form in the Esquisse; unsure

ideas.what: Matching levels before gluing by partial erasure (lowering the level) or uniform refinement ('surmarquage').
ideas.modern_name: Change of level / passing to a common refinement of finite-index structures

missed.claim: Topological structures with Z/rZ-torsor levels at boundary circles are glued only when the levels agree, the set of gluings being a torsor R_a ∧ R_{a'}. This is exactly the combinatorial shape of the balanced-node condition and the μ_r of gluing choices/ghost automorphisms for twisted stable curves (Abramovich–Vistoli), formulated topologically in 1983. It is also the shape of level structures at nodes in log/r-spin settings.
missed.quote: on suppose r(a)=r(a'), si a'=σ(a) ... un élément de R_a ∧_{Z/rZ} R_{a'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests that Grothendieck's 'Teichmüller tower with levels' is a topological precursor of the stack of twisted curves. A modular-operad formulation of the Teichmüller tower with Z/r level data could link GT-action studies (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura) with twisted-curve moduli. This is a mild, plausibly unremarked historical link.

deep.surprise_reason: Gluing in the Teichmüller tower is known from the Esquisse. The explicit torsor-level gluing condition (equal r, gluing datum in a contracted product) is a neat unpublished detail anticipating twisted-curve gluing data. However, it is short and fairly natural once the setup is given.
